question: Who among the following is worshipped as Nataraja before many classical dance performances in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shiva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shiva, known as Nataraja, is worshipped as the divine cosmic dancer before many classical dance performances in India.
 
• The term Nataraja translates to "King of Dance" (nata meaning dance, and raja meaning king).
 
• The Nataraja form of Shiva is depicted with four arms, dancing within a circle of flames, symbolizing the cosmic cycles of creation and destruction.
 
• Shiva's dance represents the dynamic and rhythmic movement of the universe and is an important motif in Indian arts and culture.
 
• Classical dance forms like Bharatanatyam and Odissi often begin with an invocation to Nataraja, seeking blessings for a successful performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iconography of Nataraja**

 
 
• The Nataraja statue typically shows Shiva dancing on the demon Apasmara, symbolizing the triumph over ignorance.
 
• His upper right hand holds a drum (damaru), representing the sound of creation.
 
• The upper left hand holds fire, symbolizing destruction and transformation.
 
• His lower right hand is in the abhaya mudra, meaning protection and assurance.
 
• The lower left hand points to his raised left foot, signifying liberation and salvation.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**
 
 
• The concept of Nataraja dates back to the Chola dynasty (9th to 13th century CE) in South India, where it became a central icon of the Chola art.
 
• Bronze sculptures of Nataraja from this period are considered masterpieces of Indian art.
 
• The Chidambaram Temple in Tamil Nadu is one of the most famous temples dedicated to Nataraja.
 
 
 
• **Philosophical Interpretations**
 
 
• Shiva's dance is seen as a symbol of the cosmic cycles of creation, preservation, and dissolution.
 
• It also represents the five activities (panchakritya): creation (srishti), preservation (sthiti), destruction (samhara), concealment (tirodhana), and grace (anugraha).
 
• The dance is also a metaphor for the inner dance of the human soul and the divine.
 
 
 
• **Role in Indian Classical Dance**
 
 
• Invoking Nataraja is a tradition in many classical dance forms like Bharatanatyam, Kathak, and Odissi.
 
• This invocation is meant to seek the deity's blessings for the success and sanctity of the performance.
 
• It also highlights the spiritual aspect of dance, viewing it as a divine art form.
